channel.title: Blockfront
channel.description: Blockfront reports crypto news: Bitcoin and Ethereum, DeFi protocols, exchanges, regulation, security incidents, funding rounds and network upgrades.

item.title: SushiSwap swaps tokens through automated liquidity pools
item.description: SushiSwap is an automated market maker: traders swap against token pools, while liquidity providers deposit assets and receive a share of trading fees.

item.title: Solana Foundation launches atomic settlement program for Solana
item.description: Solana Foundation released an MIT-licensed escrow program that settles asset and payment legs atomically; it is seeking design partners before production.

item.title: Arbswap users should check a pending swap before retrying
item.description: A pending or failed swap does not always mean the same thing: check its transaction state, nonce and wallet activity before trying Arbswap again on Arbitrum.

item.title: Fairshake backs 32 House candidates, sets $6 million for six
item.description: Fairshake named 32 House candidates for midterm support, including six getting $1 million each, after the Senate blocked the crypto market-structure bill.

item.title: Fairshake backs 32 House candidates after crypto bill stalls
item.description: Fairshake named 32 House candidates for midterm support, with six set to receive $1 million each as the crypto industry's market-structure bill remains stalled.

item.title: BNB Chain charts: when to share zoom across tokens
item.description: Per-token zoom keeps BNB Chain charts readable on their own; shared zoom aligns time windows for comparing moves, but can obscure tokens with shorter histories.

item.title: Ethereum Foundation launches zkAPI for private API payments
item.description: Ethereum Foundation and Open Anonymity launched zkAPI on Oct. 1, letting users fund AI API use on Ethereum without linking payments to prompts.

item.title: How to Reconcile BNB Chain Payouts With a Treasury Ledger
item.description: Reconcile BNB Chain payouts by matching transaction hashes, token contracts and wallet movements first, then record fees, timing and the valuation method.

item.title: Three checks for TRON Energy on unknown selectors
item.description: For an unfamiliar TRON contract method, verify its ABI signature, simulate the exact call, then treat the Energy estimate as a moving ceiling, not a quote.

item.title: Why a token can block a swap router
item.description: A token can reject a swap router through pause, blacklist or transfer rules; allowance and liquidity are separate checks, so a good quote can still fail.

item.title: Why Manta Bridge Deposits Wait After Ethereum
item.description: Manta deposits wait for Ethereum confirmation and message delivery; rollup batches publish L2 activity for data availability, not a separate deposit approval.

item.title: Manta Bridge withdrawals: how state roots affect your exit
item.description: Manta Pacific withdrawals depend on a state root that can be verified on Ethereum; knowing the stages helps you tell a pending exit from a failed one.

item.title: How to Trace a Crypto Swap Route
item.description: A swap route is a sequence of token trades across pools; compare the final amount, fees, price impact and transaction limits before signing on-chain.

item.title: Blast to wind down Ethereum layer-2 after TVL falls 98%
item.description: Blast will wind down its Ethereum layer-2 after costs outpaced revenue; users can withdraw through its interface until Oct. 26 before using Ethereum bridge contracts.

item.title: Polygon PoS withdrawals need a checkpoint and an Ethereum claim
item.description: Polygon PoS withdrawals burn tokens on Polygon, wait for an Ethereum checkpoint, then require a separate claim; the burn transaction hash tracks the transfer.

item.title: How to audit Manta withdrawal release proofs
item.description: Manta withdrawal proofs connect an L2 message to an output root; check the transaction, inclusion proof and Ethereum portal state before calling a release complete.

item.title: SEC proposes conditional crypto self-custody rules for advisers
item.description: The SEC proposed crypto custody rules on Oct. 1 that would let advisers hold client assets when no qualified custodian is available, subject to safeguards.

item.title: Why Account Funding Delays Cross-Chain Payouts
item.description: Account funding can delay cross-chain payouts because deposits must clear source-chain checks before a swap executes and destination funds can be signed and sent.

item.title: Why a token trade shows as a contract call in your wallet
item.description: A token swap often shows as a contract call because your wallet asks a smart contract to trade assets; learn what the request, approval and receipt mean.

item.title: Wallet Swap or Exchange for a TRC-20 Token?
item.description: A wallet swap keeps a TRC-20 trade on TRON, while an exchange matches orders off-chain; compare fees, custody, liquidity and withdrawal needs before choosing a route.
